g.text: Every prompt is also a potential injection. Every retrieved doc is also a payload.
Every plugin call is a privileged action triggered by natural language.
OWASP LLM TOP 10 v1.0 (Aug 2023) + v2.0 (Nov 2024) DIFF

div.style: font-size:23px; line-height:1.45; color:#1f1a14; font-style:italic; font-family:Fraunces, Georgia, serif;

foreignObject.div: The same property that makes LLMs useful — they act on unstructured text — is what makes them attackable. Securing an LLM application requires a different mental model than securing a Spring controller.

svg.text: § 01 — OWASP TOP 10 v1.0, GROUPED BY PIPELINE STAGE
LLM05 v2 — Improper Output Handling (was LLM02)
The decision tree the lecturer collapses
Each maps to an OWASP category
Two rules, three vocabularies, one forward link

g.text: ① Every text input is also a control-flow input. Prompt injection has no SQL-injection-style clean fix.
② Default-deny on agent actions. Excessive agency is what turns a model mistake into a real-world incident.
③ Self-supervised ≠ semi-supervised. GPT pre-training derives its own labels from the data.
④ RLHF is reinforcement learning, not “semi-supervised.” It’s the alignment step after pre-training.
⑤ Semi-supervised proper = some labelled + many unlabelled, with a specific algorithm class.
Session 3 opens with “ANN is a supervised problem.” This session defined what that means.
Source: OWASP Top 10 for LLM v1.0 (Aug 2023); v2.0 (Nov 2024) diff layered on top.
